True Elements is a Pune breakfast and snack food brand run by brothers-in-law Puru Gupta (CEO) and Sreejith Moolayil (COO). They first ran an aggregator of healthy food brands, then a corporate wellness business, before launching True Elements in 2017.

The range covers rolled and steel cut oats, muesli, granola, seeds such as chia, pumpkin and flax, seed and trail mixes, dry fruits, millets and snacks. The brand moved from private label to making all of its own products in 2018, at a factory in Pune that The Better India says turns out over seven lakh products a month.

Marico bought about 54% of the company in May 2022. The brand lists full ingredients on its packs and says buyers can trace an ingredient's journey on its website using the product name and batch number.

slides.text: Kerala banana and tapioca chips made with Nendran bananas and fried in rice bran oil.

Upperi is a Kochi snack brand making Kerala banana and tapioca chips. Its founders say they could not find a packaged version of the chip they grew up with, decided in June 2025 to make it themselves, then signed a manufacturing agreement and had all five flavours tested by an NABL-accredited laboratory before the first packs left their Kochi warehouse.

The brand says it uses Nendran bananas for its banana chips and Kerala tapioca for its tapioca chips, fries both in rice bran oil, and seasons them with spices. It states that it uses no palm oil and no artificial additives.
There are five flavours, three banana (Classic Salted, Masala Twist, Barbeque) and two tapioca (Peri Peri, Sweet & Spicy), each sold at ₹69 for 70 g through its own online store.

Snacks with no added preservatives (chips, chivda, makhana, traditional snacks) plus kitchen staples such as cold-pressed oils, organic grains, flours and spices.

WellBe is a packaged food brand of the Nimida Group, led by founder and director Gaurav Manchanda, and is marketed by Sowparnika Retail Private Limited of Bengaluru. The wider group also works in retail, consumer goods, farming and sports.

WellBe started in 2020 in 13 stores of The Organic World in Bengaluru. By FY 2023-24 it said it was in 1,000 stores across Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Vizag and Vijayawada, through chains such as Lulu, Spar, Spencer's and More.

Its range is built around South Indian and other traditional snacks such as kodbale, murukku, chakli, nippattu and chivda, plus makhana, chikkis and bars. In October 2025 it added vacuum-cooked snacks made from legumes, pulses and tubers, along with new items such as peanut chikki bites, Maddur vada, namak para and potato chips.

Noodles and pasta made from whole wheat, lentils, oats, chickpeas and other grains, with no maida.

WickedGud is the noodle, pasta and wrap brand of 100Percent Nourishment Pvt. Ltd., registered in CBD Belapur, Maharashtra. Founder and CEO Bhuman Dani started it in 2021, after selling his earlier tea and coffee startup, TGL Co., to Ness Wadia.

The brand says its noodles and pasta are made from whole wheat, lentils, oats, chickpeas and other grains, without maida, palm oil or artificial colours, and that it checks its nutrition figures with food technologists and nutritionists. It ships across India and to the UAE, Nepal, Australia and New Zealand.

Entrepreneur India reported in December 2025 that the brand uses a steaming and convection air drying process and is sold on Amazon, Blinkit, Instamart, Zepto, BigBasket and Flipkart, as well as in more than 5,000 retail stores including Reliance Smart Bazaar and DMart. It also launched a ₹20 masala noodle pack for general trade.

Whole, powdered and blended spices, plus dry fruits and whole food products.

ZOFF Foods, run through Asquare Food & Beverages Pvt Ltd, was started in Raipur in 2018 by brothers Akash and Ashish Agrawal, who call themselves the Spice Brothers. It sells whole, powdered and blended spices, dry fruits, and 5 minute gravy and marinade mixes.
The company says it runs a fully automated manufacturing unit in Raipur that uses cold grinding to keep the flavour and aroma of the spices, and packs them in multi-layered zip-lock packs.

ZOFF says its products are sold on major e-commerce sites and in over 10,000 retail stores across India, and that 60% of its factory staff are women. It reports revenue of ₹80 crore in 2023 and projects ₹180 crore for 2026.
